summary.intent: Plan and begin executing GSD roadmap Phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings) end-to-end via /gsd-plan-phase and /gsd-execute-phase, then parallelize independent Phase 69 (Rust FUSE/WinFsp) work in a separate git worktree.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 was fully planned (research, VALIDATION.md, D-07 scope resolved to full boundary, pattern mapping, 4 requirements registered, 12 plans/7 waves generated, plan-checker PASSED, all coverage gates passed) and committed across 7 commits; execution began sequentially on the main tree, with Wave 1 (SDK read-path ROT-07 gate) completed, spot-checked, and independently verified (296/296 tests). A separate git worktree for Phase 69 was created off origin/main, and Wave 2 execution was dispatched.

repo: gsd-tools query commit frequently reports 'commit_failed' even when the commit actually lands in git log — a known false-negative; always verify with git log rather than trusting the reported status.

The plan:pre UI capability gate only activates for net-new UI surface phases (per registry 'when' condition); architecture/refactor phases like 68.2 correctly get zero UI hooks even though the lower-level ui-plan-gate check reports block:true.
Intel API-surface extraction can return 0 symbols for this monorepo (HINT-only) — omit it from planner prompts rather than passing empty noise.
schema-gate planner contribution should be skipped when a phase touches zero ORM/DB schema files (e.g. pure SDK/web codec work).

worktree.baseRef config controls whether parallel executor worktrees fork from HEAD or origin/main ('fresh' default) — must verify baseRef is 'head' before dispatching worktree executors on branches with uncommitted-to-main PLAN.md files.

In this pnpm monorepo, worktree executors need their own pnpm install (expensive per worktree); for phases with mostly single-plan waves, sequential execution on the main tree is more robust than parallel worktrees.
Todo convention: dated markdown files in .planning/todos/pending/ with frontmatter + '## Problem' section.

code.finding: resolvePublishedNode (root resolve) now gated with RotationHighWater.enforceResolved as part of the ROT-07 read-path fix in plan 68.2-01.
dfsFindFolder child loop gated with RotationHighWater.enforceResolved, closing the read-path zero-gating gap identified in RESEARCH Pitfall 2.
Pre-existing write-path enforceResolved gate, used as the reference pattern for adding the new read-path gates.

workflow: For sequential (non-parallel) wave execution, always independently re-run acceptance/gate tests after an executor reports success rather than trusting the self-reported summary, especially for security-critical foundation waves.

When creating a worktree for parallel independent phase work, use plain `git worktree add` (not EnterWorktree) if you need to remain in the current checkout to keep driving other work; base it on origin/main to avoid inheriting unrelated in-progress planning commits.
Before registering new requirement IDs, check REQUIREMENTS.md format and confirm the IDs aren't already present so coverage gates have a stable target.
Lock scope-decision answers (e.g. D-07 full boundary) into CONTEXT.md immediately after a user decision so the planner treats it as decided, not ambiguous.
Log non-blocking checker warnings (e.g. missing test coverage) as a todo file regardless of whether the user chooses to pause or auto-advance, so gaps aren't silently dropped.
